dicas.texto: Para encontrar a porcentagem, precisamos que o denominador seja 100. Por qual número multiplicamos 25 para chegar a 100?
Você identificou o fator de escala correto (4). Agora, aplique esse mesmo fator ao numerador (28) para manter a equivalência.
Tente decompor a conta: quanto é 20 vezes 4 e quanto é 8 vezes 4? Depois, some os dois resultados.
Você está quase lá! 20 x 4 = 80 e 8 x 4 = 32. Agora, basta somar 80 + 32 para encontrar o novo numerador.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: Think of the numerator as the number of dogs and the denominator as the kennel capacity.
For each row, enter the number of dogs first and 25 cages second.
The three rows use 25 dogs for Total, 28 dogs for Part 1, and 7 puppies for Part 2.
Fill the six cells from left to right as the Total pair, the Part 1 pair, and the Part 2 pair, using the dog count over 25.
Ask whether 100 is larger or smaller than 25.
Compare the target denominator with the original denominator and choose multiplication for an increase.
The denominator must change from 25 to 100 in every row, not from 100 down to 25.
Select the multiplication symbol in both operation menus of each row.
A scale factor tells how many times the original denominator must grow.
Find the factor by dividing the target denominator, 100, by the original denominator, 25.
Use the same factor for the numerator and denominator in each row because equivalent ratios preserve their value.
Calculate 100 divided by 25, then enter that factor in all six scale-factor cells.
Equivalent ratios require the numerator and denominator to change by the same factor.
Multiply each original numerator by the scale factor 4.
Compute 25 groups of 4 for Total, 28 groups of 4 for Part 1, and 7 groups of 4 for Part 2.
Use repeated addition of four equal groups or multiplication by 4 for each numerator, then enter the three products in row order.
When a ratio has denominator 100, its numerator tells how many percent are represented.
Read the numerator of each equivalent ratio whose denominator is already 100.
The three numerators over 100 are 100, 112, and 28 in row order.
Copy each numerator over 100 into its percentage cell and keep the same order: Total, Part 1, then Part 2.

exercicio.statement:
Abhi works at a kennel that has cages for 25 dogs, assuming one dog per cage. Sometimes, it gets very busy and he has to put multiple dogs in the cages as needed.

Part 1) If 28 dogs were dropped off, the kennel was filled to what percent capacity?

Part 2) If instead 7 puppies were boarded, how busy was the kennel in terms of percent capacity? Part 1) If 28 dogs were dropped off, the kennel was filled to what percent capacity?
Part 2) If instead 7 puppies were boarded, how busy was the kennel in terms of percent capacity?

hints.message: When a ratio has denominator 100, its numerator tells how many percent are represented.
Read the numerator of each equivalent ratio whose denominator is already 100.
The three numerators over 100 are 100, 112, and 28 in row order.
Copy each numerator over 100 into its percentage cell and keep the same order: Total, Part 1, then Part 2.

misconceptions.description: O aluno usa uma fração de referência (50%) como resposta padrão para qualquer problema de porcentagem.
misconceptions.feedback: 50% means half of the capacity. These rows must be read from the calculated ratios over 100, so do not use 50% as a default.
